name: Desktop OS
description: Operating systems for daily-driver desktop and laptop computing, judged on what a user can actually accomplish out of the box and beyond.

name: Startup Banking
description: Business banking and card platforms for venture-backed and bootstrapped startups, judged on payments, spend controls, yield, and how well they plug into accounting and AI-driven finance workflows.

name: Project Management
description: Team planning and tracking tools for software and product organizations, judged on how well they support planning, collaboration, reporting, and automation without becoming their own full-time job.

name: Web Scraping APIs
description: Hosted extraction and browser-automation APIs for turning arbitrary web pages into clean, structured data at scale, judged on extraction quality, anti-bot resilience, and developer ergonomics.

name: Mobile AI Dev Tools
description: iOS and Android apps that let developers write code, run terminals, and manage infrastructure from a phone or tablet, judged on connectivity, git integration, and how well they support running coding agents on the go.

name: Code Hosting
description: Git hosting and collaboration platforms, judged on repo management, CI/CD, project planning, self-hosting options, and how well they support agentic and automated contribution workflows.

name: AI Coding Agents
description: AI-powered coding assistants and autonomous agents, judged on code generation quality, codebase understanding, autonomy, IDE/terminal integration, and safety of unsupervised changes.

name: Edge & App Platforms
description: Deployment platforms for shipping web apps, APIs, and functions close to users, judged on how far the free/hobby path goes, edge compute and data primitives, and how well they plug into agent-driven build and deploy workflows.

name: Frontend Frameworks
description: JavaScript UI frameworks and their surrounding toolchains, judged on component and reactivity models, runtime performance, ecosystem depth, and how well they support AI-assisted and agentic development.

name: Local LLM Runtimes
description: Tools for running large language models on your own hardware, judged on model support breadth, performance across CPU/GPU/Apple Silicon, API compatibility, quantization flexibility, and fit for agentic and power-user workflows.

name: Payroll & HR Ops
description: Payroll and HR operations platforms for startups and growing companies, judged on running payroll end-to-end, contractor and global payments, tax filing and compliance, onboarding and benefits, and how well payroll plugs into accounting systems and agent-driven workflows.

name: Product Feedback & Intent
description: Tools that capture user feedback and product intentions and turn them into prioritized, buildable work.

name: Software Factory
description: End-to-end autonomous software production: systems that turn product intent into implemented, reviewed, shipped code with minimal human handholding, judged on spec fidelity, autonomous PR quality, and how much oversight they still require — distinct from interactive pair-coding agents that sit in a human's editor.

name: Mobile & In-Person Payments
description: Platforms for accepting in-person and mobile card payments — Tap to Pay on off-the-shelf phones, dedicated readers and smart terminals, and the APIs behind them — judged on how fast a merchant can start taking payments, checkout and fleet-management depth, offline resilience, payouts and reconciliation, and how well agents can drive the whole stack.

name: API platforms
description: API clients, testing tools, and gateways for designing, mocking, testing, documenting, and operating APIs, judged on collection workflows, spec-driven design, traffic management, team collaboration, and how well agents can drive them.

name: Team Chat
description: Team messaging and collaboration platforms, judged on channel and thread models, search, calls, workflow automation, app-platform and bot depth, compliance and exports, and how well agents can read and post through official APIs and MCP servers.

name: Backend as a Service
description: Hosted backend platforms bundling database, realtime sync, auth, storage, and serverless functions, judged on data and security models, local development, migrations and type safety, vector search, and how safely an agent can provision and evolve a backend end-to-end.

name: Online Payments
description: Online payment platforms for accepting cards and wallets, running subscriptions, and moving money at scale, judged on integration speed, checkout and billing depth, payouts and reconciliation, disputes and fraud tooling, and how completely an AI agent can drive the money flow end-to-end.

name: Accounting & Bookkeeping
description: Accounting and bookkeeping platforms for startups and small businesses, judged on the core ledger workflows (chart of accounts, bank feeds and reconciliation, invoicing and bills, financial statements, month-end close), accountant collaboration, and how much of the ledger an AI agent can read and post to programmatically.
